inquilina.g: The woman renting the room, with a contract until the thirtieth.

contrato.g: The rental agreement that fixes the dates and the money.

prazo.g: The time limit the contract sets before it ends.

caução.g: The deposit left with the landlord, returned when the contract ends.

diária.g: The price of one night in the rented room.

metrô.g: The underground city train she now lives beside.

resolvo.g: I sort it out (resolver), said with more confidence than she has.

resolve.g: You sort out (resolver), here as a question about how.

gastou.g: Spent, used up all the money (gastar).

arruma.g: Tidies, puts in order (arrumar); here, what is already tidy.

arrumado.g: Already tidy, in order; the past participle of arrumar.

quebram.g: Break, and about money, leave someone with nothing (quebrar).

levantar.g: To raise, here to raise the voice in anger.

vejo.g: I see, I look at it (ver); here, I will deal with it tomorrow.

segunda-feira.g: Monday, the first working day of the Brazilian week.

reunião.g: The work meeting where the routes are given out.

rotas.g: The travel routes the agency sells, each with its towns.

rota.g: The travel route a seller is given to sell.

às.g: At, used with the hour: at nine, at seven.

agência.g: The travel agency where she sells trips.

pasta.g: The flat case she carries the work papers in.

marginal.g: The wide fast road along the river in São Paulo.

trânsito.g: The traffic, all the cars moving or stopped.

motoboy.g: A courier on a motorbike, weaving between the cars.

retrovisor.g: The car mirror that shows what comes from behind.

abriu.g: Opened, and about traffic, started moving again (abrir).

adiante.g: Further ahead, further along the road.

bainha.g: The folded edge at the bottom of her trousers.

calça.g: Trousers, covering the legs from waist to feet.

encharcada.g: Soaked through, with the water inside the cloth.

norte.g: The north of the country, the route she wanted.

chefe.g: The boss who runs the meeting and hands out routes.

pauta.g: The list of points the meeting has to get through.

subi.g: I went up, here up the river (subir).

conheço.g: I know, from having been there (conhecer).

chegou.g: Arrived, got there (chegar); here, too late.

sobrou.g: Was left over, nobody else wanted it (sobrar).

interior.g: The inland towns, away from the coast and the capital.

quiser.g: If you want, said about a choice still open (querer).

hotel.g: The place travellers sleep, here one without a pool.

piscina.g: A swimming pool, the thing this hotel does not have.

guarda-chuva.g: The umbrella she opens against the rain.

perna.g: The leg, where she presses the wet umbrella.

mapa.g: The map she opens to count the towns.

cidades.g: Towns, the eleven she has never sold.

vendeu.g: Sold, gave to a buyer for money (vender).

olhando.g: Looking at, keeping her eyes on it (olhar).

gosta.g: Likes it, and here it is the whole ending (gostar).

turno.g: The work shift she starts at seven.

emprestado.g: Borrowed, lent to her for the trip and to give back.

colega.g: A workmate, someone she works with but not a close friend.

caminhão.g: A lorry, the big vehicle that fell across the road.

tombou.g: Fell over onto its side and stayed there (tombar).

engarrafamento.g: The traffic jam, cars in a line that does not move.

der.g: If it works out in time, from dar, about having enough time.

pego.g: I take, I catch, here a later flight (pegar).

temporada.g: The season, the months when the rain comes every year.

despedida.g: The goodbye, the moment before someone leaves.

vou.g: I go, I am going (ir); here, on foot.

chego.g: I arrive, I get there (chegar); here, sooner walking.

pisca-alerta.g: The blinking car lights that warn the drivers behind.

desce.g: Gets out, gets down from the car (descer).

acostamento.g: The strip at the side of the road where cars stop.

buzina.g: Sounds the horn (buzinar); the car behind is impatient.

graça.g: The funny side of something; here there is none.

guarda.g: Keep it for me, save it (guardar); said as a request.

dezembro.g: December, the month she asks him to keep a place for.

garoa.g: Fine cold drizzle that soaks you slowly.

curitiba.g: Curitiba, a cold, orderly city in the south of Brazil.

encharca.g: Soaks it through (encharcar), slowly and completely.

pensão.g: A cheap guest house with rooms rented by the night.

nova.g: New, the one she has just been given (novo).

cobradora.g: The woman who takes the fares at the bus station.

terminal.g: The big station where the city bus lines start.

sinal.g: The phone signal, which her room does not get.

copos.g: Cups, the two she brings out to the corridor (copo).

sou.g: I am (ser); here, yes, that is me.

aparelho.g: The phone itself, the thing held to the ear.

ouvido.g: The ear, where she keeps the phone too long.

toma.g: Have some, take it (tomar); an offer, not an order.

cafezinho.g: Small strong coffee offered to anyone who comes by.

estou.g: I am, right now (estar); here, in the middle of a call.

ligação.g: A phone call, from the moment it starts until it ends.

espero.g: I will wait (esperar), said by someone who does not.

orelha.g: The outer ear, against which the phone stays.

estação-tubo.g: Curitiba's glass tube stop, where buses are boarded.

ia.g: Was going to (ir); here, was about to miss it.

anota.g: Writes it down (anotar) so as not to forget.

cartão.g: The plastic card you touch to pay for the bus.

catraca.g: The metal bar you push through once you have paid.

saldo.g: The money left on a travel card.

recarrega.g: Top it up (recarregar), put credit on the card.

real.g: The Brazilian currency; here, the one coin she is short.

quentinho.g: Nice and warm, said of bread straight from the oven.

saiu.g: Left, went out (sair); here, the bus is gone.

próximo.g: The next one, the one that comes after this.

van.g: A small shared van that charges more than the bus.

lotada.g: Completely full, with no space left inside (lotado).

tubo.g: Short for the tube stop, what everyone here calls it.

veste.g: Puts on a coat or clothes (vestir).

casaco.g: A warm coat for going out into the cold.

chave.g: The small metal thing that opens a door or gate.

barigui.g: Barigui, the big park with a lake in Curitiba.

parque.g: Green public space where people walk and rest.

geada.g: Thin white frost that covers the ground at dawn.

pinhão.g: Pine nut, roasted and eaten hot in southern Brazil.

assado.g: Roasted, cooked over heat until it is done.

endurece.g: Goes hard (endurecer), so you cannot bite it.

dente.g: A tooth, used here to break the shell open.

disse.g: Said, told (dizer); here, nobody said it.

aprende.g: Learns by doing it (aprender), the way everyone does.

junho.g: June, the middle of the southern winter.

serra.g: The cold hill country away from the coast.

pátio.g: Open yard beside the house, where the fire is lit.

tabela.g: A sheet with the prices set out in rows.

fumaça.g: Grey smoke rising from the fire, carrying the smell.

brasa.g: Red hot coal under the meat, with no flame.

cozinha.g: The room where the food is cooked.

galeto.g: Young chicken grilled on a spit, the Sunday dish here.

gira.g: Turns round and round (girar), here over the fire.

espeto.g: Long metal stick the meat is turned on.

família.g: The people you belong to, here all at one table.

comprida.g: Long, made for many people to sit along (comprido).

genro.g: The man married to somebody's daughter.

piada.g: Short funny story told to make people laugh.

dialeto.g: The local way of speaking, brought by the old families.

atrasada.g: Late, behind the others by a moment (atrasado).

percebe.g: Notices something the others do not see (perceber).

entendeu.g: Did you understand? (entender), asked straight out.

palavra.g: A single word, the smallest thing you can say.

admite.g: Says something true that makes her look bad (admitir).

travessa.g: Wide dish that food is carried to the table in.

prateleira.g: Shelf on the wall where the dishes are kept.

baixado.g: Put down, lowered (baixar); here the knife and fork.

talher.g: Knife, fork and spoon, the tools you eat with.

pouquinho.g: A tiny bit more, said when offering food again.

obrigada.g: Thank you, said by a woman.

sério.g: Honestly, really; she means the no.

tia.g: Aunt, and any older woman of the family.

frase.g: Sentence, the words somebody says in one go.

molho.g: Thick liquid poured over meat or pasta.

afrouxa.g: Loosens something that got too tight (afrouxar).

cinto.g: Strap around the waist that holds trousers up.

vinho.g: Wine, made here in the valley by the families.

jarra.g: Big open jug that a drink is poured from.

rótulo.g: Paper label on a bottle saying what is inside.

próprio.g: His or her own, belonging to that person.

aconselha.g: Tells her what she should do (aconselhar).

estava.g: It was, in the past (estar); here, praise for the dish.

ótimo.g: Very good, the word used to praise a dish.

fome.g: The feeling of needing to eat soon.

elogiar.g: To say out loud that something was very good.

colheradas.g: Spoonfuls, as much as a spoon holds (colherada).

gesto.g: A movement of the hand or body that says something.

valia.g: Was worth more (valer), counted for more.

escrito.g: Written down, in letters on paper or a lid.

barbante.g: Thin string used to tie a box shut.

através.g: Through, coming out from the other side.

protesta.g: Says out loud that it is far too much (protestar).

volto.g: I come back (voltar), said as a promise.

salame.g: Dry sausage in thin slices, made in these valleys.

colonial.g: Farm made, the old way of the settler families.

geleia.g: Sweet fruit spread kept in a glass jar.

tampinha.g: Small lid that screws onto the top of a jar.

cuca.g: Sweet crumb cake from the German and Italian south.

volume.g: How much space a piece of luggage takes up.

quilos.g: Kilos, what the scales count in (quilo).

excesso.g: More weight than the airline allows.

informa.g: Tells her the fact she needs (informar).

despacho.g: Handing luggage over so it flies in the hold.

comissão.g: The part of the sale the seller keeps.

etiqueta.g: Small printed label stuck on a bag before a flight.

alça.g: The handle you hold a bag or a box by.

fixa.g: Fixed, always the same from now on (fixo).

cais.g: The stone edge of the town where boats tie up.

pesca.g: Fishes, catches fish (pescar); here before dawn.

ilhas.g: Islands, the land out in the bay (ilha).

vaga.g: A free place, one more seat on the boat.

maresia.g: The salt smell the sea leaves on everything near it.

casco.g: The body of a boat, the part in the water.

encostado.g: Leaning against the pier, resting there and still.

píer.g: Wooden walkway going out over the water.

cabo.g: Thick rope that holds a boat against the pier.

calcula.g: Works the numbers out in her head (calcular).

carona.g: A free ride somebody gives you in their boat or car.

enrolando.g: Winding the rope into a coil (enrolar).

âncora.g: Heavy metal hook that holds a boat in one place.

incomodada.g: Uneasy, not comfortable with what just happened.

travessia.g: The crossing from one shore over to the other.

boia.g: Floating marker showing where the deep water runs.

queixo.g: Chin, used here instead of pointing a finger.

trajeto.g: The way taken from one place to another.

encurta.g: Makes it shorter (encurtar), here the crossing.

dobrados.g: Folded over, the notes kept in a pocket (dobrado).

canal.g: Channel of water, what the street becomes at high tide.

limo.g: Green slime the water leaves on stone and wood.

ontem.g: Yesterday, the day just before today.

peguei.g: I caught it (pegar); here, a fish.

robalo.g: Sea bass, the fish these boats bring in at dawn.

venda.g: Small corner shop that sells a bit of everything.

derrotada.g: Beaten, having given up trying to win (derrotado).

favor.g: Something helpful done with nothing asked back.

devolver.g: To give a thing back to the person it came from.

presente.g: Something given without being paid for.

retribui.g: Pays a favour back with another favour (retribuir).

esquecer.g: To stop having a thing in your mind at all.

gentileza.g: A kind act done with nothing asked back.

pescador.g: Man who lives by catching fish from a small boat.

apelido.g: Short name friends use instead of the real one.

rotina.g: The same thing happening again at the same hours.

cobrança.g: Asking somebody for the money that they owe.

deve.g: Owes it still, has not given it back (dever).

esfria.g: Gets cold, the way coffee does when left (esfriar).

torrado.g: Toasted, browned by heat until it is crisp.

movimento.g: How many customers come into a shop or a hotel.

fraco.g: Weak, with far fewer people than usual.

maio.g: May, a quiet month between the busy seasons.

planilha.g: Sheet of rows and numbers used to track the money.

ilha.g: Island, the land people cross the bay to reach.

marmita.g: Packed lunch carried in a tin or plastic box.

sublinha.g: Draws a line under it so it stands out (sublinhar).

reserva.g: A place kept for somebody in advance.

falha.g: Lets somebody down, does not turn up (falhar).

compromisso.g: Something promised for an agreed time.

ganho.g: I get in return (ganhar); here, nothing.

caderno.g: Notebook with lined pages for writing things down.

açougueiro.g: The man who cuts and sells the meat in town.

embarque.g: The moment when passengers get onto the plane.

mensagem.g: Short written message sent from one phone to another.

curta.g: Short, said of an answer with very few words.

pago.g: Paid, settled; here the debt is over.

sublinhado.g: Underlined, with a line drawn under it.

folheto.g: Printed sheet an agency uses to sell a trip.

subo.g: I go up (subir), here with the group.

adverte.g: Warns her before it goes wrong (advertir).

cantil.g: Metal water bottle carried on a long walk.

furado.g: Full of holes, so it cannot be trusted.

lotação.g: The most people a trip can safely take.

posto.g: Small station at the start of the trail.

capacidade.g: How many people it can hold at one time.

descascando.g: Flaking off, the way old paint does (descascar).

autorização.g: Written permission to take groups into the park.

assinada.g: Signed by hand, so it counts (assinado).

vistoria.g: Official check that everything is as it should be.

norma.g: Rule that everybody working here has to keep.

penalidade.g: What you pay if you break the rule.

exigência.g: Something demanded before you are allowed to go.

pagas.g: Paid for already, by people who are waiting.

responsabilidade.g: Being the one who answers if things go wrong.

prejuízo.g: Money lost on a deal that did not work.

viva.g: Alive, in one piece at the end of the day.

estorna.g: Pays the money back for a cancelled booking (estornar).

naquela.g: On that one, in that same afternoon.

multa.g: Money you must pay for breaking a rule.

cume.g: The very top of the mountain.

animado.g: Cheerful and full of energy at the start.

pisa.g: Puts her foot down on it (pisar).

raiz.g: Part of a tree that comes up through the path.

ajoelha.g: Goes down on her knees beside her (ajoelhar).

apalpa.g: Feels the hurt place with her fingers (apalpar).

calada.g: Saying nothing on purpose for a while (calado).

entorse.g: A twisted joint, hurt but with no bone broken.

feias.g: Bad ones, worse than they look (feio).

chia.g: Makes a hissing noise instead of a voice (chiar).

chamo.g: Shall I call? (chamar), asked in the moment.

socorro.g: Help, called for when somebody is badly hurt.

chamada.g: A call made from a phone or a radio.

resgate.g: A team coming up to carry an injured walker down.

maca.g: Flat bed with handles for carrying a hurt person.

dupla.g: Two people working together on the same job.

improvisa.g: Makes it on the spot from what is there (improvisar).

tala.g: Stiff piece tied on to stop a joint moving.

compressa.g: Cold wet cloth pressed onto a swollen place.

repartido.g: Shared out, carried by more than one person.

inchaço.g: The swelling that comes up after a joint is hurt.

bota.g: Strong closed shoe for walking on wet rock.

enfermaria.g: Small room where hurt people are looked after.

curativo.g: Bandage put on to hold or cover an injury.

pronto.g: Ready, done and in place at last.

seguro.g: Insurance, what pays when something goes wrong.

apólice.g: The paper that says what the insurance pays for.

alívio.g: The good feeling when a worry goes away.

tornozelo.g: The joint between the leg and the foot.

folha.g: Sheet of paper waiting empty on the table.

passado.g: Just made, poured through the filter (passar).

dita.g: Says the words out loud for her to write (ditar).

enrola.g: Winds the rope into a coil (enrolar).

rascunho.g: Rough first version written before the final one.

revisão.g: Going over a text again to correct it.

gráfica.g: The shop that prints the sheets and posters.

botar.g: To put a word in, to add it to the text.

cachoeira.g: Falling water on a river, where walkers swim.

aventura.g: Exciting trip with some danger; the word that sold.

gruta.g: Cave in the rock that walkers go into with lamps.

caneta.g: Pen, the one whose ink goes through the paper.

lista.g: Set of short lines written one under the other.

duplo.g: Double, done twice over the very same place.

impressas.g: Printed onto the paper by a machine (impresso).

reclamação.g: A customer saying out loud that something was wrong.

fechar.g: To close, here the boot over a swollen foot.
